counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 101, '2023-01-01'); -- Author views their own article INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (2, 102, 103, '2023-01-02'); -- Author views another user's article
explanation: Q1 filters views where the author and viewer are the same, while Q2 attempts to join the VIEWS table with itself on the condition that the author ID matches the viewer ID, which is incorrect and leads to unintended results.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should include cases where an author views their own article (author_id = viewer_id) and cases where an author views another user's article (author_id != viewer_id). The difference in results will be in the DISTINCT IDs returned by each query.
